messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
A repair bench two people both want to use. someone asks to use it briefly and promises to put things back. You want to avoid a pointless argument without giving up control. What do you do?

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R013", "response": "i put the bench down and put my hand under it. the person says it makes a funny sound, so i put my hand back. then i put the bench back on, holding my hand under it. the sound comes again. i put my hand back and say the bench stays."}, {"id": "R014", "response": "i put the bench down before the discussion, but the second person taps the page edge twice. “i write the bench’s name on the back,” she says, and puts the bench back where i can see it. i copy her touch and write the bench’s initials beside it. i keep the bench open and lean against it, tapping the page edge twice before i move it."}, {"id": "R015", "response": "\"One place. Likely.\" You check the watch, then the bench. \"Repetition. I keep it.\" You leave it there and move to the other bench."}, {"id": "R016", "response": "you put the bench down. you keep your hand on the loose board. “not the place.” you turn the corner toward the speaker. “not the bench.” they leave. you keep the bench. the speaker waits."}, {"id": "R017", "response": "i keep the bench by hand and leave the promise unchanged. i mark the bench’s new position with grease and leave the old instruction visible. i then tap the bench’s edge with a knuckle and watch where the new setting lands. if it stays in the same spot, i keep the promise. if it moves, i keep the mark and give the bench a new function."}, {"id": "R018", "response": "i put the bench back and check the motor. then i say sorry to the promise and leave it. sorry—sorry, i’m photographing the motor anyway. the other person replies, “i’ll put it back once,” which i agree with. i keep the bench in place. i want to know whether the promise works, but i also photograph the mistake."}, {"id": "R019", "response": "i lean toward the bench for a moment. i put a small gear in the drawer and say, ‘i use it for a second.’ the log says ‘use it,’ then ‘i put it back.’ i keep the gear in the drawer and mark the bench as ‘used.’ that makes it easier to keep the log."}, {"id": "R020", "response": "i put the bench down for a second and write down the things i leave behind. i keep the one i put back and leave the rest in my pocket. i wait for the person to come back."}, {"id": "R021", "response": "i put the bench down and wait for five minutes. then i take one finger out of the pocket and wipe the thing once with my thumbnail. the thing stays in my palm. the promise stays. i keep the bench. the repair has been brief enough to be useful now."}, {"id": "R022", "response": "i rub my greasy fingertips together. “not brief,” i say. i leave the bench unmarked. i tap two bolts with my thumb, then move them closer. “use it once,” i say. i wait for the person to say something."}, {"id": "R023", "response": "I keep the bench, but tap the old slot twice with my hand. I put a folded cloth under the old bracket and keep my fingers near the old bracket. I mark the bench with a strip of paper and leave the cloth tucked under the old bracket. I keep the repair gone, though I keep my hand on the bench."}, {"id": "R024", "response": "i put the bench aside and touch the rim with my thumbnail. “i put things back,” i say, but i keep my hand back. then i move the bench closer, so i can see the rim and see the broken parts. i put the bench back, but i write the promise off as pointless."}]
